data.name: Masheer
data.gender_notes: Masheer is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root sh-r-r, meaning 'lion'. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'mas'hara', meaning 'a lion'. In Islamic tradition, lions are symbols of courage, strength, and nobility. The name Masheer carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Masheer usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual warrior who is determined to overcome challenges and obstacles on the path to enlightenment.
data.etymology: Masheer belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Masheer total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar', written around 1377–1406 CE, mentions Masheer as a town in the Maghreb region, belonging to the Zanata Berbers. The name Masheer is stated to be derived from the Arabic word 'maashi', which means 'stones'. The town was significant due to its fertile land and strategic location, making it a target for various Islamic dynasties throughout history.

Al-Idrisi's 'Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Ikhtiraq al-Afak' (The Pleasurable Journey to the Ends of the Earth), written around 1154 CE. This geographical work describes Masheer as a city near the Mediterranean coast, belonging to the Zirid Dynasty. The name Masheer is mentioned as derived from the Arabic word 'maashi', which means 'horses'. The city was significant due to its agricultural wealth, especially its production of horses and grapes.
